old = '''"""Certified feature-window export planning.

The epoch is expressed as the certificate circulation of PROTOCOL.md.  The
eligible (slot, window) arcs are factorised through a segment tree over the

equivalent to the published one for values, certificates and cuts.

new = '''"""Certified feature-window export planning.

The epoch is expressed as the certificate circulation of PROTOCOL.md and
solved exactly in three stages:

1.  Maximum coverage.  Feasibility of the flow lower bounds ceil(r*target) is
    a Hoffman circulation condition, tested by a maximum flow between an
    artificial source (group/sink nodes carrying the forced amount) and an
    artificial sink (flow nodes).  A binary search over the finite ratio set
    Rset yields the optimal r; the residual reachability set of the failed
    test at the next ratio is the required infeasibility cut.
2.  Optimal utility and waiting age.  With cost (time_s - ready_j) -
    value_j*W on the service arcs, W = 1 + J*last slot time makes one utility
    unit dominate the whole achievable age range, so a minimum cost
    circulation is exactly the lexicographic (utility, age) optimum.  It is
    obtained by saturating every window arc (an extreme flow), which leaves
    node imbalances, and routing them with successive shortest paths; the
    maintained node potentials are the residual optimality certificate.
3.  Reporting.  Window assignments are recovered by decomposing the service
    tree flows; slot, flow and group arc flows are read off directly.

The eligible (slot, window) arcs are factorised through a segment tree over
the slot indices so a window contributes O(log S) arcs instead of O(S).  Tree
and attachment arcs carry unbounded capacity, so the factorised network has
the same feasible assignments, the same optimum, and its potentials imply the
published arc conditions by summing along the tree path of an eligible pair.
"""'''
assert old in src
open('planner.py','w').write(src.replace(old, new))
